business: SEGMENT: short-term rental, Santa Cruz County
prompt_text: I need a vacation rental in Santa Cruz County. Which specific rental companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: What are the best vacation rentals in Santa Cruz County California and how do I pick one?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you a short, practical list now — then I can tailor it (and pull phone numbers/links) if you tell me your dates, budget, party size, location preference and whether you need pet- or disability-friendly housing.

Top companies/platforms to call (and why):

1. Airbnb
   - Why: Largest inventory of private homes, condos and unique stays in Santa Cruz County; excellent filters (entire place, self-check‑in, pets); many recent guest reviews to evaluate hosts; good for flexible/short notice bookings.

2. Vrbo (formerly HomeAway)
   - Why: Focuses on whole-home rentals and family stays; lots of beachfront and single-family houses listed in Santa Cruz/Capitola/Aptos — good if you want privacy and kid-friendly features.

3. Booking.com
   - Why: Broad mix of hotels, apartments and vacation homes; often has instant booking and free cancellation options; good for comparing hotel vs. rental pricing quickly.

4. Vacasa
   - Why: National professional property manager that often operates in coastal markets — consistent standards for cleaning, linen, 24/7 guest support and clear policies (good if you want reliability and onsite management).

5. TurnKey Vacation Rentals (or other professionally managed networks)
   - Why: Professionally managed homes with standardized quality, digital check-in, and local support — useful if you prefer hotel-like consistency but want a full home.

6. Local property managers / visitor resources (call the Santa Cruz County Visitors Bureau / Visit Santa Cruz County)
   - Why: Local managers and the county tourism office know neighborhood-specific permit rules, peak-season nuances, and often have exclusive local listings (Capitola, Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk area, La Selva Beach, Davenport, Aptos). They can also confirm short-term rental permits and transient occupancy (TOT) compliance — important in this market.

How to prioritize who to call first
- If you want the widest selection and user reviews: start with Airbnb and Vrbo.
- If you want professional management and reliable service: call Vacasa or TurnKey.
- If you want local, neighborhood-specific help (Capitola, Aptos, La Selva, Watsonville): contact the Santa Cruz County Visitors Bureau or ask for local property managers — they’ll know permit rules and have off-platform listings.

What to ask when you call (so you get the right place)
- Exact location / distance to the beach or downtown
- Maximum occupancy and bedrooms/bathrooms
- Pet policy and extra fees
- Cleaning fee and cancellation policy
- Whether they’re permitted/registered with Santa Cruz County (short-term rental permit)
- Check-in/check-out logistics and 24/7 support
- Any extra charges (TOT, parking, linens)

If you want, tell me:
- travel dates, number of guests, pets, budget, and your preferred area (Santa Cruz city, Capitola, Aptos, Davenport, etc.), and I’ll pull up specific local property managers and phone numbers and recommend a short list to call.
